**Yes.** The story mostly stretches time. It lingers on small, nearly real-time actions: the jammed key, the dust on her thumb, the rusty water, the drips fading out, the curtains drawn one by one. This slow pace fits the subject, a woman hesitantly re-entering her late mother's house. It conveys her reluctance and grief and builds quiet unease around the cellar door.

The one compression, "Seit zwanzig Jahren hatte sie sich eingeredet…", folds two decades into a single sentence. It supplies the needed backstory without breaking the slow, present-moment rhythm. Sensory detail, brief memory (the mirror) and restraint (not approaching the cellar) are well proportioned, so the pacing serves the atmosphere and nothing feels rushed or padded.
